summary: The audit checks the 111 units: every 1L required course, a 1L discussion course, a spring elective of 3-8 LAW units, and 81 units of electives from LAW courses or the pre-approved non-law list, with at most 31 units from courses outside the Law School. You move in the courses designated Experiential Learning (8 units), ethics, R paper and Professional Writing, which also count as electives. Checked by hand: that one course does not cover more than one of R, ethics and EL (EL with PW is allowed), that externships, directed research and writing, theses, the research track, moot court, Trial Lawyer Skills, Law Journal Discussion Group and outside courses together stay within 31 units, non-law courses not on the list, the learning outcomes requirement, and nine to twelve quarters in residence.

wzmIwGQX.why: "JD students must complete all first-year required courses, plus an additional 81 approved quarter units of elective coursework": LAW courses (now in the course data) and the pre-approved non-law courses listed under Optional Approved Non-Law Courses. "Students must complete 8 units of coursework designated as fulfilling the Experiential Learning (EL) requirement"; "JD students must complete at least one advanced course that contains one or more units of ethics instruction"; "all students must complete one course of at least two units ... (an 'R' paper), and one course of at least two units ... (a professional Writing 'PW' course)." EL, ethics, R and PW are designations on courses counted in the electives, so they share; designations are not in the course data, so the student moves each course in. "Students cannot use a single course to satisfy the 'R,' 'Ethics,' and/or 'Experiential Learning' requirements" (except EL with PW) is checked by hand.

0WJ3Eg5p.why: "34-46 Units": a unit range heading for the quarters below, not a separate requirement.

pE7pXolC.why: "65-75 Units": a unit range heading for the 2L and 3L years; their requirements are in the graduation requirements.

mJLvqpu3.why: "During Winter Quarter they may take no more than 5 units of electives." A limit, not a requirement.

y52ksZrd.why: "Complete any LAW course from 3-8 units" and "During Spring quarter they must take 3-8 units of electives"; these are part of the 81 elective units, so the rule shares its course.

f3YkdV8L.why: "Optional Approved Non-Law Courses": the non-law courses that count as approved electives. Every one is an item of the 81-unit elective rule, so this list is information, not a requirement of its own (as a rule it asked a student who took no non-law course for one).

totals.label: Courses outside the Law School (at most 31 units count toward the 111)
totals.why: Policies: "JD students may not count toward the JD graduation requirement more than thirty-one (31) quarter units of the following types of coursework: externship, directed research, directed writing, senior thesis, research track, courses taken outside the Law School, moot court (Kirkwood competition), Trial Lawyer Skills Workshop, and Law Journal Discussion Group." Units of courses outside the Law School past 31 do not count toward the 111; the shared limit with the LAW courses in the list is checked by hand.
